_comment: Copy to config.json. That file is gitignored: it names real phone numbers, and this is a public repository. Every key is optional and every default is the restrictive one.
_audience: everyone:true means anyone who messages this number is answered, and every inbound message becomes untrusted input to an agent holding a shell. That is the configuration Tulip is designed for and the one docs/THREAT-MODEL.md assumes. Set false to fall back to the numbers list.
_operators: Who may run ! control commands and who receives watchdog alerts. NEVER widened by audience.everyone. Bare international digits, no + and no spaces. Leave empty and you have no way to hold delivery or block someone from your phone.
_groups: Off by default. A public assistant added to a group answers people who never chose to talk to it, in a room whose history it cannot see. replyTo 'mention' answers only a real @mention or a reply; 'trigger' also answers on a trigger word.
_limits: Abuse and cost control. Turns are the expensive unit — each is a model call — so turnsPerDay is the ceiling one person can put on your bill. messagesPerHour and burst shape the rate; the burst exists so someone typing four short lines in a row is not throttled for being human.
_panel: The control panel can read every message and hold delivery, and it authenticates with one bearer token. Loopback by default; reach it over an SSH tunnel rather than binding it wider. If you do expose it, put something that authenticates in front.
_delivery: debounceMs collects a burst of quick messages into one prompt. maxBatch caps how many are handed over at once; the rest wait for this chat's next turn in the rotation.
